relevance_note: Case series of 17 HA20 patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants in which several are named with individual detail, e.g. "two patients received a diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) at 8 years according to DSM-5 (p7, p14)".
method_note: Read the whole Markdown by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I chose and checked spans. No supplementary material is in the file (online supplemental files 1-3 with per-patient genetics, clinical data, pedigrees and therapies are not included), and Table 1 and the therapy paragraph are group-level only. Scope: the cohort is 17 patients from 6 families, all with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants; rows were made only for the 11 cohort members the text names individually (pt1-pt4 of family 1, p7, p10, pt13, p14, pt15, Pt16, pt17). The other 6 cohort members are never named or individually described, so they get no rows (counted in n_patients_reported/cohort_size_as_stated). Labels are verbatim: the paper writes 'p7', 'p10', 'p14' but 'pt13', 'pt15', 'pt17', 'pt1'-'pt4', and 'Pt16' (sentence-initial, only form used). Three previously published individuals mentioned in the Discussion were included under label rule 4 (superscript reference numbers written without the caret): Duan et al ref 31 (de novo TNFAIP3 frameshift, NPSLE), ref 32 (T674P variant, progressive neuroinflammation, baricitinib) and the proband of the ref 36 family (cutaneous disease; same TNFAIP3 variant as one of this paper's families, variant not printed). Group-level studies (Yu et al 61 patients, Aeschlimann et al 16, Elhani et al 177, the 16-patient SLE cohort of ref 9, the other members of the ref 36 family) got no rows. Cohort variants: per-person variant descriptions are only in figure 1/supplement, so variant_original_string is 'not reported'. The text mentions 'pArg183Ter' and a de novo deletion of exons 7-9 but does not tie either to a family or patient, so neither was attributed; variant type ('truncating variants resulting in stop codon', one being a CNV) and inheritance ('All but one variants were inherited') are not attributable per person and were left 'not reported'. European ancestry, heterozygosity, ACMG class 4-5 and genetically confirmed HA20 diagnosis are stated for all 17 patients and were applied to each named cohort member. Ref 31 is called 'de novo' without any statement of parental testing, so inheritance was left 'not reported' (rule 8). T674P was recorded in protein_hgvs_as_stated although printed without 'p.'. Neuropsychiatric diagnoses (ADHD, anxiety, mood dysregulation, ODD, pica, depression) were recorded as features but not mapped to the checklist item 'central nervous system involvement', which I left 'not reported' for cohort patients; NPSLE (ref 31) and progressive neuroinflammation (ref 32) were mapped to it as observed. One of Pt16/pt17 had a suicide attempt ('leading in one case to suicide attempt') but the paper does not say which, so it was not recorded. The seven named neuropsychiatric patients account for all seven with neuropsychiatric symptoms, but no exclusion was inferred for pt1-pt4 because the paper gives only a count, not an explicit named-group negative statement. The CXCL9/10 finding previously described 'in a family' (ref 8) was not attributed to family 1 individuals because it is family-level. No internal contradictions found.
